value.title: Submit verification
value.summary: Stop the UI claiming a submit it cannot prove, and never double-submit a prompt.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Exit zero from tmux proves bytes moved, not that the agent accepted them — pij had to add composer polling for exactly this. GATED ON oq-0004: whether the standing never-capture-pane constraint binds product code or only agents and tests. Built last so that answer can arrive late.

value.title: Verify the submit by reading the pane the drawer is driving
value.success: After a submit, the code can tell whether the payload is still pending in the composer.
value.notes: GATED ON oq-0004 — proceeding on the recorded reading (agents and tests never run capture-pane; product code may read the pane it is itself driving), because without it the UI can only report exit codes, which workshop 001 section 5 proves are a lie. INHERITED FROM PHASE 2, do not rediscover: (1) Any new websocket control frame MUST be added to CONTROL_TYPES in hooks/use-terminal-socket.ts — a frame missing from that Set is not rejected, it is written into xterm as terminal data and prints raw JSON into the user's terminal. Your verification frame will hit this. (2) The send-keys branch sits inside the JSON.parse try in terminal-ws.ts; an escaping throw falls through to pty.write(data), so assert nothing reaches the pty even when the runner throws. (3) Capture with -J (capture-pane -p -J) or wrapped lines break any string match. (4) There is deliberately NO success signal to build on — terminal-inner toasts on failure only, and the send result field is named so no UI can accidentally assert success from a zero exit. Phase 3 supplies the FIRST honest success signal this feature has; do not weaken that by reporting success on anything short of an observed submit.
value.note: HELD on oq-0004 by ruling of pij-chief-roadrunner 2026-08-09: phase 3 is SPLIT so no part of it bets on an unruled reading. This task is the pane read and is entirely oq-0004's; tk-0202 does not depend on it and is being built now. If Jordan rules no, tk-0202 survives untouched and the honest fallback is a UI that claims nothing — still strictly better than today. If he rules yes, nothing is lost by having built the independent half first. Same pattern as phase 1 being deliberately send-free.

value.title: At-most-once re-press, and the negative half of honest UI state
value.success: Enter is re-pressed at most 3 times at 250ms while a payload is still pending, the payload is NEVER retyped, and no success is ever signalled from an exit code alone.
value.notes: BUILDABLE NOW — independent of oq-0004. Two halves, and only the negative one is in scope until the pane read is ruled. (1) AT-MOST-ONCE: re-press Enter up to 3 times at 250ms, NEVER retype the payload after the first Enter — retyping is how a prompt gets double-submitted, and at-most-once beats speculative replay (workshop 001 section 2). Without the pane read there is no pending signal to drive the retry, so build the mechanism and its policy with the signal injected, so tk-0201 can supply it later without reshaping this. (2) THE NEGATIVE HALF OF HONEST UI: assert that nothing claims success from a zero exit code. Phase 2 deliberately ships no success signal — terminal-inner toasts on failure only — and this task must keep it that way rather than adding one. Exit 0 proves bytes moved, not that the agent accepted them (workshop 001 section 5). INHERITED FROM PHASE 2: any new websocket control frame MUST be added to CONTROL_TYPES in hooks/use-terminal-socket.ts or it is written into xterm as terminal data and prints raw JSON into the user terminal; and the send-keys branch sits inside the JSON.parse try in terminal-ws.ts, so an escaping throw falls through to pty.write.

tk-0201.assertion: A pending payload is distinguishable from a consumed one after Enter.

tk-0202.assertion: An inconclusive verification yields at most 3 Enter re-presses at 250ms and ZERO additional type or paste calls.
tk-0202.receipt: Verified at send-prompt-keys.ts:272-284 — the loop body is sleep, probe, Enter only. M11 (retype before each re-press) reddened 2 tests; M11b (re-paste the buffer) reddened 3 including the paste path; M13 (budget raised past the constant) reddened 3.

tk-0202.assertion: No success is reported on a zero exit code alone.
tk-0202.receipt: Three assertions: sender resolves undefined; submitting-path ws reply is exactly {type, delivered}; no file handling delivered emits toast.success. M16 (toast.success on delivered) and M18 (reply grows ok:true) both reddened. The third is a SOURCE SCAN, named as one in its own doc comment because the decision lives in an inline closure jsdom cannot render — weaker evidence than a behaviour test, and said so rather than letting the name imply otherwise.

tk-0202.assertion: The re-press loop stays inside the per-pane queue, so a second send cannot type between a retry probe and its Enter.
tk-0202.receipt: M12 (loop moved after the queue releases) reddened exactly one test — the worst-form assertion, where the retry submits the WRONG prompt because its licence was granted about a payload no longer there.
